Summary: The DRAGIN framework paper proposes a novel dynamic RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) framework that optimizes when and what to retrieve based on the real-time information needs of large language models (LLMs). It introduces two key components: RIND (Real-time Information Needs Detection) to determine when to retrieve and QFS (Query Formulation Strategy) to decide what to retrieve. The paper evaluates DRAGIN on four knowledge-intensive datasets using three different LLMs, showing state-of-the-art performance and outperforming existing dynamic RAG methods. The framework addresses the limitations of current dynamic RAG methods by making intelligent, adaptive retrieval decisions based on the internal states of Transformer-based LLMs.
